title: 第46章 今天这条街就是我的战场
content_zh:
第46章 今天这条街就是我的战场-《重生80，分家后带妻女吃香喝辣》

店里的客人纷纷抬起头，往窗外看。

“咋了咋了？外面出啥事了？”

“不知道啊，听着像是有人在打架？”

“打架？大中午的打什么架？”

林国强的动作顿了一下，手里的铲子停在半空。

他侧耳听了听，眉头微微皱了起来。

那声音不对。

不是打架，打架的声音不是这样的。

那些尖叫声里带着一种东西，是恐惧。

是那种见了什么可怕的东西之后，控制不住的恐惧。

“志军，快出去看看。”他喊了一声。

赵志军放下手里的碗，在围裙上擦了擦手，跑到门口，探出脑袋往街上看了一眼。

只一眼。

他的脸“唰”地白了，像被人抽干了血一样。

脑袋“嗖”地缩回来，整个人像被烫了一样，退了好几步，后背撞在门框上，发出“咚”的一声闷响。

“三、三姐夫……”他的声音都在抖，“外面有个疯女人，拿着刀，见人就砍！”

店里的客人全站了起来，椅子被推得吱嘎乱响。

有人冲到门口往外看，有人缩到角落里，有人把钱往桌上一拍就要往外冲。

“别出去！”林国强一声低吼，所有人都停住了。

他放下铲子，关了火，从灶台后面走出来。

他的动作不快，但每一步都很稳，不像别人那样慌慌张张的。

“志军，把卷帘门拉下来。”

赵志军伸手就去够卷帘门的拉绳，手抖得厉害，抓了好几次才抓住。

“等等。”林国强忽然按住了他的手。

赵志军愣住了：“三姐夫？”

林国强站在门口，透过门缝往外看。

街上已经乱成了一锅粥。

人们四散奔逃，卖菜的老太太扔下了菜筐，推自行车的丢下了车子，一个小孩摔倒在地，被大人一把拎起来夹在腋下继续跑。

满地的白菜帮子、碎鸡蛋、翻倒的竹筐、歪倒的自行车，还有一只不知道谁跑掉的棉鞋，孤零零地躺在路中间。

街对面，一个中年女人正挥舞着一把菜刀，追着一个男人砍。

那女人四十来岁，穿着一件灰扑扑的棉袄，头发散乱，像一蓬枯草。

她的脸上没有任何表情，眼睛直勾勾的，瞳孔涣散，嘴巴半张着，口水顺着嘴角往下淌。

The customers in the store raised their heads and looked out the window.

"What's going on? What's going on outside?"

"I don't know. It sounds like someone is fighting?"

"A fight? What kind of fight is this at noon?"

Lin Guoqiang paused for a moment, and the shovel in his hand stopped in mid-air.

He listened carefully and frowned slightly.

That sound wasn't right.

It's not a fight, that's not what a fight sounds like.

There was something in those screams, fear.

It's the kind of uncontrollable fear that comes after seeing something scary.

"Zhijun, go out and take a look." He shouted.

Zhao Zhijun put down the bowl in his hand, wiped his hands on his apron, ran to the door, stuck his head out and took a look at the street.

Just one glance.

His face turned pale, as if his blood had been drained.

His head retracted with a "swish", and his whole body seemed to be burned. He took several steps back, and his back hit the door frame with a muffled "thunk" sound.

"Third, third brother-in-law..." His voice was trembling, "There is a crazy woman outside with a knife, and she will kill everyone she sees!"

All the customers in the store stood up and their chairs creaked.

Some people rushed to the door and looked out, some shrank into the corner, and some people slapped their money on the table and rushed out.

"Don't go out!" Lin Guoqiang roared, and everyone stopped.

He put down the shovel, turned off the fire, and stepped out from behind the stove.

His movements were not fast, but every step was steady, not as hasty as others.

"Zhijun, pull down the rolling shutter door."

Zhao Zhijun stretched out his hand to reach for the pull cord of the rolling shutter door. His hands were shaking so much that he had to grab it several times before he could catch it.

"Wait." Lin Guoqiang suddenly held his hand.

Zhao Zhijun was stunned: "Third brother-in-law?"

Lin Guoqiang stood at the door and looked out through the crack in the door.

The streets have become a mess.

People fled in all directions. The old lady selling vegetables dropped her vegetable basket, the bicycle pusher dropped his car, and a child fell to the ground. An adult picked him up and put him under his arm and continued running.

There were cabbage sticks, broken eggs, overturned bamboo baskets, tilted bicycles, and a cotton shoe that ran away from someone unknown, lying alone in the middle of the road.

Across the street, a middle-aged woman was wielding a kitchen knife and chasing a man to chop.

The woman was in her forties, wearing a dusty cotton-padded jacket, and her hair was as messy as a pile of withered grass.

There was no expression on her face, her eyes were straight, her pupils were dilated, her mouth was half-open, and drool was dripping from the corners of her mouth.
